**Finding submitted: missing (high severity, confidence 0.85)**

- **Issue:** Article IV (¶p0049) locks Licensee into a 36-month initial term, renewable for a further seven years *at Licensor's option*, with no convenience-exit right anywhere in the Agreement. The only termination mechanics are Licensor-favourable: immediate termination on any Licensee breach (¶p0049, ¶p0043), automatic termination on Change of Control (Art. XX), wind-up (¶p0137), and mutual insolvency (Art. XIX).
- **Classification:** No customer convenience right in a multi-year term is walk-away territory under T4C — it fails both the preferred and fallback positions. Licensor holds no convenience right either, so the gap runs one way only.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** New clause IV inserted after Article IV, giving Licensee a 30-day convenience termination right with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees and no early-termination penalty, per the playbook model language; 60 days' notice flagged in the comment as an available fallback.
